newsitem.title: THAILAND: Christiani Thai sees 2.54 bln baht loss.
newsitem.headline: Christiani Thai sees 2.54 bln baht loss.

text.p: Christiani and Nielsen (Thai) Plc managing director Suthep Phansomboon said on Monday the company's restructuring costs will push it's 1996 loss to 2.537 billion baht.
Suthep told an analysts meeting the loss includes restructuring costs of 1.764 billion baht and write downs on construction work costing the company 786.8 million baht.
Christiani expects operational losses this year of 258 million baht ($10.32 million).

Suthep said the losses were due to a slowdown in European construction where Christiani's Copenhagen-listed subsidiary Christiani and Nielsen A/S operates. It was also affected by unbalanced and rapid growth, mismanagement and a lack of internal controls.
Christiani said it has bad debts of 149 million. The company's interest repayments this year will total 312 million baht. Revenues in 1996 are estimated at 11.554 billion baht.

A rescue plan by financial advisor National Finance and Securities sees Christiani raising 2.245 billion baht from a five for seven share rights issue, and a further 712 million baht from an issue of five-year, no coupon, convertible debentures.

The company's holding in profit-making German subsidiary property developer Nobleclear GmbH will drop to 18.91 percent from 80.74 percent as Chrisitiani has decided not to subscribe to a rights issue.

Christiani will also sell some its subsidiaries UK developers Sunway and Stanford, as well as firms owned by Christiani subdsidiary Harmony. It will borrow 67 million marks through associate Newco at the end of this year.
The company will also implement further internal cost-cutting measures.
Christiani's assets at the end of 1996 are forecast to total 6.297 billion baht with liabilities of 5.615 billion baht. The company is carrying retained losses in 1996 of 3.567 billion baht.
Christiani aims to increase income from infrastructure projects from a current 3.0 percent to 60 percent of total revenues over the next 18 months.

With the support of key shareholders, which include the Thai Crown Property Bureau, the plan forecasts that Christiani will return a profit of 68 million baht on revenues of 11.7 billion baht in 1997.
